lines: I remember being lost from the flock. You brought me back to the fold.
My thoughts were all tangled wool. You helped card them straight.
You helped pull me back when even my name felt far away.
I remember the weakness afterward and your hand keeping the cup steady.
Your voice was the first thing that made sense when the fever broke.
I woke under a blanket I knew, but nothing else felt familiar yet.
You stayed through the worst of it. I have not forgotten that.
The village told me what you risked. Parts of me remember it too.
I can work the loom again because you did not give up on me.
When I see you, I remember warmth returning to my hands.
I was afraid I would never recognize the flock again.
You gave me time when I could barely form a thought.
The cure hurt, but it gave me my mornings back.
I still have bad nights. Knowing I came back helps.
My family got me back because you stepped in.
I owe you thanks that a trade discount cannot quite carry.
The first wool I touched afterward felt like proof I was myself.
I remember you telling me to hold on. Somehow, I did.
You saw a villager in me before I could see one in myself.
If you ever need shelter here, you will have it.
Your face feels familiar, soft in one place and snagged in another.
I remember shivering, then warmth returning one thread at a time.
The memory is rough around the edges, but your face stayed in it.
Were you the one by the bed, or did someone tell me that afterward?
I know I should thank you. I am still fitting the reason together.
Some mornings I remember the cure clearly. Today is not one of them.
Your voice brings back a room, a bowl, and the taste of something bitter.
I remember running from you. I do not remember why.
There are gaps where whole days should be.
I woke knowing the sheep by sound but not the people around me.
Did I hurt anyone while I was sick? No one gives me a straight answer.
I can picture your hands mixing the cure, though the room around them is gone.
My mind keeps returning pieces in the wrong order.
You were there when I came back. That much feels certain.
The bell sounded strange for days after I woke.
I remember being terribly hungry and too frightened to eat.
Please do not take it badly if I ask your name again.
The cure ended the sickness. The confusion took longer.
I know this village is home, even when it feels borrowed.
Tell me what happened slowly. I want the truth, not comfort.
I remember you through panic and wool-dark dreams. Keep your voice low.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left echoes behind. Stand where I can breathe around them.
Do not come any closer. I remember enough for that.
You saved me, but my body still expects danger when I see you.
I know the cure worked. That does not make the memory gentle.
Give me a moment before you ask for gratitude.
I remember being trapped and your face above me. Both things can be true.
You did what had to be done. I am not ready to speak kindly about it.
Keep your hands where I can see them.
The shaking starts before I can remind myself who you are.
I woke cured and terrified. The second part has not fully passed.
I do not want to discuss those days beside a crowded pen.
Thank you for helping. Now please give me room.
Some nights I hear that groan in my own breathing.
The village trusts you. I am trying to catch up.
I remember the weakness more clearly than the rescue.
Do not tell me I am safe. Let me decide when I feel it.
I can face you today. That is as much as I can offer.
Leave the door clear while we talk. I need to know I can walk away.
